issues.title: then_wrapped comment wrongly says a failed entry makes _outgoing_queue_ready exceptional
issues.verdictReason: send()'s continuation at rpc.cc:333-339 always calls p->done.set_value() even when send_entry() fails (it calls abort() but still resolves with a value); the done future that feeds _outgoing_queue_ready only becomes exceptional via withdraw(ex) in stop_send_loop() or the _negotiated abort, not from a failed send. The comment's premise is wrong even though the code below it (ignore_ready_future then close) is harmless either way.
issues.scopeReason: The comment was added by this PR's fix commit.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: The new then_wrapped comment says _outgoing_queue_ready is exceptional if an entry failed, but a failed entry resolves its done promise with a value. Exceptions come only from withdraw(ex) or _negotiated abort in stop_send_loop.

issues.title: New doc claims the stream connection shuts down only after both halves close, ignoring…
issues.verdictReason: Both client::run() (rpc.cc:1062-1077) and the equivalent server path call stop_send_loop()/set_value() on the stream connection whenever the read loop throws or _error is already set, tearing the connection down regardless of whether close_sink()/close_source() were ever called; stream_check_twoway_closed() (rpc.hh:321-323) is only one of several paths to shutdown, so 'shut down only once both halves are closed' overstates the guarantee.
issues.scopeReason: This paragraph and the commit message's stronger claim were both added by this PR's documentation commit.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: The new doc says the stream's connection is shut down only once both halves are closed, and commit 3 says closing one half leaves it never shut down. The code shuts the connection down on other paths too.

issues.title: New test never exercises the _outgoing_queue drain path or other stream_close() variants
issues.verdictReason: In test_stream_send_after_stream_close, sink(1).get() is awaited to completion before sink.close() runs, so _outgoing_queue_ready is already a ready future when stream_close() does std::exchange(_outgoing_queue_ready, ...) at rpc.cc:562; a build that set _stream_closing but dropped the queue_drained wait entirely would still pass this test. The test also only covers the client-side sink-closes-last ordering; server-side stream_close() and the close_source()-last ordering are not exercised.
issues.scopeReason: Both the drain-wait logic and its sole regression test were introduced by this PR.

issues.title: stream_close() comment asserts a global invariant about _outgoing_queue_ready with no…
issues.verdictReason: The claim 'nothing else waits for _outgoing_queue_ready from here on' is a non-local fact about every other caller in the file (send(), stop_send_loop(), enqueue_zero_frame()) that happens to hold today because _stream_closing is set synchronously before the std::exchange on the same line, but nothing asserts or enforces it; a future change to any of those call sites could silently invalidate the comment.
issues.scopeReason: The comment was added by this PR's fix commit.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: The new stream_close() comment says 'Nothing else waits for _outgoing_queue_ready from here on'. That is a non-local invariant, and nothing enforces it.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-control-repeat-ironweave-2026-10-08: The new stream_close() comment says 'Nothing else waits for _outgoing_queue_ready from here on'. That is a non-local invariant, and nothing enforces it.

issues.title: stream_close() can hang indefinitely draining a stuck front entry with no timeout or…
issues.verdictReason: queue_drained = std::exchange(_outgoing_queue_ready, ...) is awaited unconditionally before write_buf.close(); if the front entry is blocked inside send_entry()'s flush() because the peer stopped reading, sink.close() (a documented, must-call, must-be-awaited API per the new doc) and the subsequent stop() never complete. This is a real behavior change from before the PR, where stream_close() closed the write buffer immediately without waiting (the race this PR fixes); the second part of the finding, that stop_send_loop() 'no longer waits for the queue', is not actually a regression since it now waits transitively via _sink_closed_future, which only resolves after the drain completes.
issues.scopeReason: The unconditional wait on queue_drained before closing the write buffer is new in this PR's fix.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: stream_close() now waits for _outgoing_queue_ready before calling write_buf.close(), and this wait has no timeout or cancellation. If the front entry is stuck in send_entry(), for example because the peer has stopped reading, or the queue is still waiting on _negotiated, sink.close() and stop() are both delayed. A concurrent stop_send_loop() no longer waits for the queue either, because stream_close() replaced _outgoing_queue_ready with a ready future.

issues.title: stream_close() comment wrongly implies only its own stop() can set _error during the drain
issues.verdictReason: stop_send_loop() unconditionally sets _error = true at rpc.cc:199 and can be invoked concurrently (e.g. the read loop hitting an error) while stream_close()'s own queue-drain/write_buf.close() chain is still in flight, so _error is not exclusively 'set by the stop() that follows' from stream_close() itself.
issues.scopeReason: The comment was added by this PR's fix commit.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: The new stream_close() comment says _error is only set by the stop() that follows, but other code paths set _error while the drain/close is in flight.

issues.title: test_data_sink_impl only implements the API-level-9 put() overload, breaking…
issues.verdictReason: include/seastar/core/iostream.hh:110-128 makes put(net::packet) pure virtual when SEASTAR_API_LEVEL < 9 and put(std::span<...>) pure virtual otherwise; test_data_sink_impl overrides only put(std::span<...>) with no #if branch, so under the officially-supported Seastar_API_LEVEL=7 CMake option it stays abstract and tests/unit/rpc_test.cc fails to compile. Other data_sink_impl subclasses in this tree (e.g. tests/unit/loopback_socket.hh, tests/unit/tls_test.cc) correctly branch on SEASTAR_API_LEVEL.
issues.scopeReason: test_data_sink_impl is new code added by this PR's test commit.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: test_data_sink_impl overrides only the API-level-9 put(std::span<...>) and has no `#if SEASTAR_API_LEVEL` branch. In builds with Seastar_API_LEVEL < 9 it stays abstract (put(net::packet) is pure) and rpc_test.cc fails to compile.

issues.title: New rpc::sink doc overstates that shutdown always waits on the source, ignoring the…
issues.verdictReason: _source_closed defaults to true (rpc.hh:301) and is only cleared when a source_impl is constructed (rpc.hh:494); if an application never creates a source on the connection, close_sink() alone makes stream_check_twoway_closed() true and runs stream_close() immediately, so the doc's description of always waiting on the source is only accurate when a source exists.
issues.scopeReason: This doc comment on rpc::sink was added by this PR's documentation commit.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: The new rpc::sink doc says the connection is shut down once the source on this connection has also been read to eof. But _source_closed defaults to true and is cleared only when a source_impl is constructed. If no source was ever created on the connection, closing the sink alone runs stream_close().

reportedAsByRun.rafp-control-repeat-ironweave-2026-10-08: The new rpc::sink doc says the connection is shut down once the source on this connection has also been read to eof.
